title: Aven and Dively v. Ohio Valley Presbytery
disposition_detail: Complaint neither sustained nor denied; remanded to Ohio Valley Presbytery to hear further from TE Hickey and create a more comprehensive Record. No merits ruling on whether Hickey's exception or paedocommunion is allowable.
first_summary: Two ministers complained that Ohio Valley Presbytery wrongly granted TE Charles Hickey an exception to the final clause of Larger Catechism 177 on admission to the Lord's Supper. The SJC neither sustained nor denied, finding the Record insufficient on his particular view, and remanded to the Presbytery for a fuller record. It did not decide whether paedocommunion or his formulation is allowable.
summary: Two ministers complained that Ohio Valley Presbytery erred by judging TE Charles Hickey's difference with Larger Catechism 177—over restricting the Lord's Supper to those able to examine themselves—as more than semantic but neither hostile to the system nor vital to religion. The SJC neither sustained nor denied the complaint. Because the Record did not sufficiently address Hickey's particular expression and rationale, the Commission remanded to Presbytery for further hearing and a fuller record. It reserved the merits, including whether this formulation of paedocommunion is allowable.

evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: SJC neither sustained nor denied; the Record was insufficient regarding Hickey's particular expression/rationale and related confessional and BCO implications; remanded to OVP to hear further and supplement the 133-page Record. Lines 225–231, 235–309, 311–398, 404–407.
